title: RAW_UNREVIEWED speculative: the lotus chapter keeps a human processing route separate from a reported natural-state route
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_UNSELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Pliny XIII.108 juxtaposes inhabitants' deliberate head-processing chain (heap-putrefy, wash-separate, dry, pound, eat as bread) with a separate reported sunset/sunrise change in the papaver-like head (compressed/covered at sunset, opening at sunrise through maturity and flower fall). The speculative constraint is to preserve the human operator and food-product route separately from the plant's reported state-cycle, even though both concern the head in one chapter. The passage does not assert a general grammatical rule or a shared physical process; no target meaning is proposed.

source_evidence.quote: **§108.** incolae capita in acervis putrefaciunt, mox separant lavando et siccata tundunt eoque pane utuntur. mirum est quod praeter haec traditur, sole occidente papavera ea comprimi et integi foliis, ad ortum autem aperiri, donec maturescant flosque, qui est candidus, decidat.

design.distinctive_constraint: Keep the incolae food-preparation event chain distinct from the reported papaver head state-cycle; do not turn adjacent clauses into one continuous operation or transfer human agency to the plant.
design.falsifier: The distinction fails if the source syntax does not separate the human processing subject/event from the reported day/night plant-state description, or if the proposal needs added steps not in XIII.108.
